title: Print and Comments
content:
What problem does this solve?
You need a way to see what your program is doing. print() sends text to the console so you can observe values while you learn.

Basic syntax
  print(value)
  print(value1, value2)

What actually happens
When Python reaches a print() call, it converts each argument to text, joins them with spaces by default, writes that text to the console, then continues with the next line. An argument is a value you pass into print() inside the parentheses.

Comments start with #. Python ignores them entirely — they are notes for humans, not instructions for the computer.

When this is useful
Use print() to check a greeting, a score, or any value you want to see. Use comments to record why a line exists.
concepts: print() writes values to the console
Text in quotes is a string — a piece of text Python should take literally
Multiple arguments to print are separated by spaces
Lines starting with # are comments and do not run

examples.title: A simple greeting
examples.explanation: The quotes mark a string. print writes that string, then a newline.

examples.title: Comments explain intent
examples.code:
# Show the starting gold amount
print("Gold:", 50)
examples.explanation: The comment is skipped. print receives two arguments — a string and a number — and inserts a space between them.

common_mistakes: Forgetting quotes around text: print(Hello) looks for a variable named Hello
Expecting comments to change program behavior — they never do

exercises.title: Predict the print
exercises.prompt: What does the following program print? Type the exact output (no quotes).
hints: print joins multiple arguments with a single space.
There is no extra punctuation added between HP: and 100.
The two arguments become one line with a space between them.

exercises.title: Greet the adventurer
exercises.prompt:
Write a program that prints exactly:
Hello, Adventurer!

Use print and a string.
hints: print() needs parentheses, and text needs quotes.
Use double or single quotes around the whole message.
A working shape is: print("Hello, Adventurer!")

exercises.title: Comment and two arguments
exercises.prompt:
Print exactly:
Gold: 50

Use print with two arguments (the label and the number). Put a real comment on the line above print that explains what the line shows.
hints: A comment starts with # and is a note for humans.
print can take two arguments: a string, then a number, separated by a comma.
Put a # comment on its own line above the print call.

tests.message: Add a comment that starts with # and explains the next line.
